column3: The Hebrew uses singular verbs for camping and fighting and does not explicitly describe a siege.
The Hebrew uses a pronoun rather than repeating Joshua’s name and retains the mouth of the sword and each soul.
The Hebrew explicitly says Horam went up.
The Hebrew says they camped against it rather than explicitly naming a siege.
The Hebrew repeats “on that day” with devoting every soul and does not explicitly repeat Joshua’s name.
The Hebrew calls the dependent settlements cities, repeats every soul, and does not explicitly repeat Joshua or Hebron as nouns in the latter clauses.
The Hebrew begins with “and,” without an explicit “finally.”
The first verb is singular, he captured, while the following striking and devoting verbs are plural; the settlements are called cities.
The Hebrew says Joshua struck the whole land rather than explicitly using a conquest verb.
The Hebrew says Joshua struck them rather than explicitly naming the area as what he conquered.
The Hebrew says at one time rather than explicitly naming a campaign.
